_comment: Targets the planner may choose from. RA in hours, Dec in degrees (J2000). interest 1-5. type drives the recipe. pipeline 'stack' is the only one the runner can do today; 'planet' and 'moon' items are skipped until those pipelines exist.

targets.name: M2
targets.title: M2 Globular Cluster
targets.display: M2: a globular cluster of 150,000 stars in Aquarius, 37,000 light years away, one of the biggest in the sky.

targets.name: M11
targets.title: Wild Duck Cluster
targets.display: Wild Duck Cluster (M11): a dense flock of a few thousand stars in Scutum, 6,000 light years away.
targets.why: One of the richest open clusters.

targets.name: M52
targets.title: M52 and the Bubble Nebula
targets.display: M52 and the Bubble Nebula: a star cluster in Cassiopeia beside a bubble blown by a hot giant star, 7,000 light years away.
targets.why: Cluster and nebula in one field.

targets.name: NGC 7293
targets.title: Helix Nebula
targets.display: Helix Nebula: the nearest planetary nebula, a dying star's shed atmosphere 650 light years away, big and faint.
targets.why: Nearest planetary nebula; needs a dark sky.

targets.name: NGC 7331
targets.title: NGC 7331 Galaxy
targets.display: NGC 7331: a spiral galaxy in Pegasus, 40 million light years away, a near twin of our Milky Way seen at an angle.

targets.name: M45
targets.title: The Pleiades
targets.display: The Pleiades (M45): the Seven Sisters, a young star cluster wrapped in faint blue dust, 440 light years away.
targets.why: The brightest cluster of the winter sky.

targets.name: M42
targets.title: Orion Nebula
targets.display: Orion Nebula (M42): the brightest star nursery in the sky, 1,300 light years away.

targets.name: M77
targets.title: M77 Galaxy
targets.display: M77: a spiral galaxy in Cetus with an unusually bright, active core, 47 million light years away.
targets.why: An active galaxy with a bright core.

targets.name: M74
targets.title: M74 Galaxy
targets.display: M74: a face-on spiral galaxy in Pisces, 32 million light years away, faint but perfectly symmetrical.
targets.why: Hard target; needs a long dark run.

targets.name: M31
targets.title: Andromeda Galaxy
targets.display: Andromeda Galaxy (M31): the nearest big galaxy, 2.5 million light years away, with its two small companions.
targets.why: The most famous galaxy in the sky.

targets.name: M33
targets.title: Triangulum Galaxy
targets.display: Triangulum Galaxy (M33): a face-on spiral 2.7 million light years away, large and faint.
targets.why: Third member of our local group.

targets.name: M76
targets.title: Little Dumbbell Nebula
targets.display: Little Dumbbell (M76): a small, two-lobed planetary nebula in Perseus, 2,500 light years away.

targets.name: NGC 869
targets.title: Double Cluster
targets.display: The Double Cluster (NGC 869 and 884): two young star clusters side by side in Perseus, 7,500 light years away.

targets.name: M34
targets.title: M34 Open Cluster
targets.display: M34: a loose open cluster in Perseus, 1,500 light years away.

targets.name: NGC 6960
targets.title: Western Veil Nebula
targets.display: Western Veil Nebula (NGC 6960), the Witch's Broom: the other half of the supernova remnant in Cygnus, behind the bright star 52 Cygni.
targets.why: Companion to the Eastern Veil already in the gallery.

targets.name: M57
targets.title: Ring Nebula
targets.display: Ring Nebula (M57): a smoke ring of gas thrown off by a dying star in Lyra, 2,300 light years away.

targets.name: M56
targets.title: M56 Globular Cluster
targets.display: M56: a modest globular cluster in Lyra, 33,000 light years away.

targets.name: M71
targets.title: M71 Globular Cluster
targets.display: M71: a loose globular cluster in Sagitta, 13,000 light years away, once mistaken for an open cluster.

targets.name: M39
targets.title: M39 Open Cluster
targets.display: M39: a sparse, bright open cluster in Cygnus, 800 light years away.

targets.name: NGC 7789
targets.title: Caroline's Rose
targets.display: Caroline's Rose (NGC 7789): a rich, old open cluster in Cassiopeia found by Caroline Herschel in 1783.

targets.name: NGC 457
targets.title: Owl Cluster
targets.display: The Owl Cluster (NGC 457): an open cluster in Cassiopeia that looks like an owl, or E.T., with two bright eyes.

targets.name: NGC 281
targets.title: Pacman Nebula
targets.display: Pacman Nebula (NGC 281): a glowing cloud of hydrogen in Cassiopeia with a dark bite taken out of it, 9,500 light years away.

targets.name: NGC 891
targets.title: NGC 891 Galaxy
targets.display: NGC 891: an edge-on spiral galaxy in Andromeda, 30 million light years away, cut by a dark dust lane.

targets.name: NGC 6946
targets.title: Fireworks Galaxy
targets.display: Fireworks Galaxy (NGC 6946): a face-on spiral 25 million light years away, famous for its record number of supernovae.

targets.name: NGC 6888
targets.title: Crescent Nebula
targets.display: Crescent Nebula (NGC 6888): a shell blown by a massive star in Cygnus that will one day explode, 5,000 light years away.

targets.name: IC 1396
targets.title: Elephant's Trunk Nebula
targets.display: Elephant's Trunk (IC 1396): a dark winding pillar of dust inside a vast glowing nebula in Cepheus, 2,400 light years away.

targets.name: NGC 7662
targets.title: Blue Snowball
targets.display: Blue Snowball (NGC 7662): a small, bright blue planetary nebula in Andromeda.

targets.name: NGC 7009
targets.title: Saturn Nebula
targets.display: Saturn Nebula (NGC 7009): a planetary nebula in Aquarius with faint side lobes that look like Saturn's rings.

targets.name: Albireo
targets.title: Albireo
targets.display: Albireo: the famous gold-and-blue double star at the head of Cygnus the swan.

targets.name: M16
targets.title: Eagle Nebula
targets.display: Eagle Nebula (M16): the star-forming cloud that holds the Pillars of Creation, 7,000 light years away.

targets.name: M17
targets.title: Omega Nebula
targets.display: Omega Nebula (M17), also the Swan: a bright star-forming region in Sagittarius, 5,500 light years away.

targets.name: M92
targets.title: M92 Globular Cluster
targets.display: M92: a bright globular cluster in Hercules, overshadowed by its neighbour M13 but nearly as fine.

targets.name: NGC 6543
targets.title: Cat's Eye Nebula
targets.display: Cat's Eye Nebula (NGC 6543): a tiny, intricate planetary nebula in Draco.

targets.name: M1
targets.title: Crab Nebula
targets.display: Crab Nebula (M1): the wreckage of a star seen exploding in the year 1054, 6,500 light years away.

targets.name: M36
targets.title: M36 Open Cluster
targets.display: M36: a young open cluster in Auriga, 4,100 light years away.

targets.name: M37
targets.title: M37 Open Cluster
targets.display: M37: the richest of the Auriga clusters, about 500 stars 4,500 light years away.

targets.name: M38
targets.title: M38 Open Cluster
targets.display: M38: an open cluster in Auriga whose brighter stars trace a rough cross.

targets.name: M78
targets.title: M78 Reflection Nebula
targets.display: M78: a blue reflection nebula in Orion, dust lit by young stars, 1,350 light years away.

targets.name: NGC 2024
targets.title: Flame and Horsehead
targets.display: The Flame Nebula and the Horsehead: glowing and dark clouds beside the star Alnitak in Orion's belt.

targets.name: M35
targets.title: M35 Open Cluster
targets.display: M35: a large open cluster at the feet of Gemini, 2,800 light years away, with a tiny second cluster beside it.

targets.name: NGC 2244
targets.title: Rosette Nebula
targets.display: Rosette Nebula (NGC 2244): a huge ring of glowing gas around a young star cluster in Monoceros, 5,000 light years away.

targets.name: Saturn
targets.title: Saturn
targets.display: Saturn and its rings.

targets.name: Jupiter
targets.title: Jupiter
targets.display: Jupiter and its four big moons.

targets.name: Moon
targets.title: The Moon
targets.display: The Moon tonight.
